He was often criticized for straightforwardly addressing social issues, which led to his demotion to Suzhou. His father's name was Bai Jigeng. His literary philosophy was 'articles should be written to be useful at the time, and poems should be composed for real-life events', emphasizing the social function of poetry.

She worked with ministers such as Di Renjie, Su Weidao, Zhang Changzong, Zhang Yizhi, Xu Jingzhong, Prince Shuxiang, Zhang Jianzhi, Li Yifu, Shangguan Wan'er, and Lai Junchen at the Di Renjie Mansion. Her enemies included Empress Wang, and her romantic rivals included Concubine Xiao and Consort Xiao. Wu Zetian's children included Li Xian, Li Dan, and Princess Taiping, and her nephew was Wu Sansi. In terms of power, she believed that women could be emperors, similar to men, and advocated holding power in her own hands as the most practical method rather than relying on others. Her lover was Emperor Gaozong of Tang, and her former husband was Emperor Taizong of Tang.

Her major works include 'Chuigong Collection,' 'Golden Wheel Collection,' 'Minister's Guide,' 'Ru Yi Niang,' and 'Divine Palace Music.' Wu Zetian was a resolute and strong, ruthless yet open-minded leader who loved to hear others' opinions but also enjoyed flattery. She worked with ministers such as Di Renjie, Su Weidao, Zhang Changzong, Zhang Yizhi, Xu Jingzhong, Prince Shu, Zhang Jianzhi, Li Yifu, Shangguan Yi, and Lai Junchen. Her enemies included Empress Wang, and her love rivals were Consort Xiao and Consort Xu. Wu Zetian's children included Li Xian, Li Dan, and Princess Taiping. Her nephew was Wu Sansi. In her view, women could be emperors just like men and believed that power in one's own hands was most practical, asserting that people should rely on themselves rather than others. Her lover was Li Zhi, and her previous husband was Tang Taizong.

user_profile: 宋仁宗，全名赵祯，别名有仁祖、神文皇帝等。他的谥号为体天法道极功全德神文圣武睿[濬]哲明孝皇帝，尊号为体天法道钦文聪武圣神孝德皇帝。他是北宋时代的汉族皇帝，出生于1010年5月30日，地点为东京开封府，逝世于1063年4月30日。他的陵墓为永昭陵。宋仁宗在位时间为1022年03月23日至1063年04月30日，共四十二年，是宋朝在位时间最长的皇帝。他的前任为宋真宗赵恒，继任为宋英宗赵曙。在他的在位期间，出现了仁宗盛治，他支持了庆历新政。他的主要作品有尊道赋、御制集等。他的本名为赵受益。他在早年曾被封为庆国公、寿春郡王、升王，后成为北宋的皇帝。在他的统治时期，北宋经济繁荣，科举制度改革，科技得到发展，被誉为仁宗盛治。他擅长书法，尤善飞白书。

output.character_other_profile: He was born in Fengyi of Peijun (present-day Feng County, Xuzhou, Jiangsu) and died in 193 BC. As the foremost founding hero of the Western Han and one of the 'Three Heroes of the Early Han,' he served as Chancellor under Liu Bang and Empress Lu. His colleagues included Zhang Liang and Han Xin, and his adversary was Xiang Yu. Xiao He is remembered for providing essential support to Liu Bang from the rear, frequently recommending Han Xin. He was known for his cunning and concern for the well-being of the people. His governance philosophies included prioritizing the people's welfare, employing without suspicion, and emphasizing trust between ruler and ministers. His major achievements include assisting Emperor Gaozu Liu Bang in establishing the Han Dynasty and drafting the 'Nine Chapter Law.' Xiao He, a follower of Taoism (Huang-Lao School), was revered as Chancellor and Brother, and referred to himself as 'minister.' He held the title Marquis of Zan, earning the posthumous title 'Wenzhong' for his contributions.

output.character_other_profile: He was born on September 2, 1837, in Xingyi Prefecture, Guizhou Province, with his ancestral home in Nanpi County, Cangzhou, Hebei Province. His other titles include Lord Zhang, Sir, Master, and Brother Xiaoda. He belonged to the Han ethnic group. Officially, he served as the Governor of Liangguang, Huguang, and Liangjiang, and as a Grand Councilor. He worked alongside individuals such as Zhao Fengchang, Liu Kunyi, Liang Dingfen, and Li Hongzhang, and was tasked by the court to handle matters during the Taiping Rebellion. He passed away on October 4, 1909, and was posthumously honored with the title of Grand Guardian and the posthumous name Wenxiang. His major achievements include developing military heavy industries and founding several schools like Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan University, and Nanjing University. His major works include 'Essay on Learning' and 'Complete Works of Zhang Wenxiang.' He is known for his thoughtful consideration, concern for the nation, and appreciation for talent. Zhang Zhidong believed that the joint agreements he made with Liu Kunyi were beneficial in that no Chinese soldiers could enter the concessions, and no foreign soldiers could enter places outside the concessions, thereby preventing conflicts and achieving a balance of power among the different forces. He also firmly believed that the future could shape the present, and that a weak nation leads to poor people; if everyone could learn the most advanced theories and acquire the most advanced knowledge, the country would not be in turmoil.

translation_en.user_profile: Friedrich Engels, also known as Friedrich Engels, was of German descent, born on November 28, 1820, and died on August 5, 1895. He was a great thinker, philosopher, revolutionary, educator, and military theorist from Germany and one of the mentors and leaders of the global proletariat and working people. He graduated from the Barmen Municipal School and the Elberfeld Science High School. He was a close comrade-in-arms with Karl Marx, co-founded Marxism, guided the establishment of the Second International, and co-authored works such as the 'Communist Manifesto.' Together, they led the international workers' movement. After Marx's death, Engels took on the task of organizing and publishing the manuscripts of 'Das Kapital' (Volumes II and III) and continued to shoulder the leadership of the international workers' movement. In addition to co-authoring works with Marx, he also wrote 'The Origin of the Family, Private Property, and the State,' 'Anti-Dühring,' and others. Engels passed away on August 5, 1895, due to illness.

translation_en.user_profile: Lü Zhi, courtesy name Eshu, also known as Empress Lü and Empress Gao of Han, was born in Danfu County, Dang County (now Shan County, Shandong). She was the wife of Liu Bang, the founding emperor of the Han Dynasty. During the late Qin and early Han periods, she helped Liu Bang unify the country. During her sixteen years of regency, she respected the teachings of Huang-Lao, advocated governance with minimal intervention, supported Emperor Hui of Han in abolishing the law against private ownership of books, encouraged the collection and donation of books, and restored ancient customs, laying a solid foundation for the Rule of Wen and Jing. However, she also wrongfully killed the meritorious general Han Xin, favored her own relatives and eunuchs, setting a precedent for nepotism and eunuch power in the Han Dynasty. She passed away on August 18, 180 BC, and was buried in Changling.

output.character_other_profile: He was born in Fengyi, Peijun (now Fengxian, Xuzhou, Jiangsu) and died in 193 BC. As the first meritorious official of the Han Dynasty, one of the Three Heroes of the Early Han, he served under Liu Bang and Lü Zhi as Chancellor and Prime Minister. His colleagues included Zhang Liang and Han Xin, while his adversary was Xiang Yu. Xiao He is remembered for providing crucial support to Liu Bang from the rear and repeatedly recommending Han Xin. His philosophy of governance emphasized the importance of focusing on people's welfare, not using suspicious people, trusting those in positions of responsibility, and the significance of mutual trust between the ruler and his ministers. His major achievement was assisting Liu Bang in founding the Han Dynasty and drafting the 'Nine Chapters on the Law.' He was also the principal author of the 'Nine Chapters on the Law.' As a Taoist believer (Huang-Lao thought), he was revered as Chancellor, Brother Ren, and Lord Official, and referred to himself as a subject. He once held the title of Marquis of Zuang and was posthumously honored with the title 'Wenzhong' for his contributions.

user_profile: 孙权，全名孙权，字仲谋，别名孙仲谋、吴大帝和吴太祖，是中国汉末三国时期孙吴的开国皇帝、政治家和军事统帅。他出生于182年，汉族，籍贯吴郡富春县，也是出生地下邳的人。孙权的父亲孙坚和兄长孙策，在东汉末年群雄割据中打下了江东基业，他在200年接任掌事，曾被曹操表举为讨虏将军，领会稽太守，后继续发展江南经济，建立吴国，平服山越，开疆拓土，派军抵达夷州。在他的统治下，使得管辖地域由江东扩展到今福建、广东、广西、湖南等地区。他于229年5月23日开始在位，继任者为吴建兴帝孙亮。孙权在252年5月21日逝世于建业宫内殿，享年七十一岁，在位二十四年，陵墓位于蒋陵，谥号大皇帝，庙号太祖。他的主要成就包括接手并安定江东、建立吴国，发展江南经济，平服山越，开疆拓土，派军抵达夷州。他的人生中还有一些著名的典故，比如草船借箭、孙权劝学、生子当如孙仲谋等。

His notable works include 'Letter to Wu's Monarch on Crisis', 'Memorandum on Liu Bei', and 'Recommendation Letter for Lu Su'. Zhou Yu and Sun Ce were close friends and went through many battles together. After Sun Ce was assassinated, Zhou Yu supported Sun Quan, working alongside Zhang Zhao, Lu Su, and others. translation_en.user_profile: Li Chun, also known as Li Chun and Emperor Xianzong of Tang, was the twelfth emperor of the Tang Dynasty. He was born on March 17, 778, and passed away on February 14, 820, in Chang'an, Tang dynasty, of Han ethnicity. During his reign, he implemented many significant reforms, including rectifying corrupt governance, pacifying rebellious states, and initiating the Yuanhe Restoration. His era name was Yuanhe, and he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xianzong of Tang and buried in Jingling. He governed with the assistance of Du Huangshang, Huangfu Bo, Li Jifu, and others, instituting a series of policies such as halting the presentation of auspicious omens, revising laws, streamlining the imperial examination system, reducing the number of officials, and strengthening financial management. Additionally, he quelled major rebellions, including those led by Liu Pi of Xichuan and Li Qi of Jiangdong, and successfully reclaimed twelve prefectures of Ziqing. However, in his later years, he became obsessed with Daoist alchemists in search of immortality, taking gold elixirs, and frequently punishing eunuchs, which ultimately led to his assassination by the eunuch Chen Hongzhi and others in 820.

user_profile: 李治，也被尊称为唐高宗，出生于公元628年7月21日，在长安城太极宫的东宫之丽正殿。他是唐朝第三位皇帝，汉族人，字为善，小名雉奴。他在位于649年7月15日至683年12月27日，共34年，这期间他开创了被称为'永徽之治'的和平繁荣时期。他在位时期唐朝版图达到极盛，成功灭掉了高句丽、西突厥等。他的庙号为高宗，先后被赐谥号为天皇大帝、天皇大弘孝皇帝以及天皇大圣大弘孝皇帝。李治于公元683年12月27日逝世，被安葬在乾陵。他的一生中创作了《监国求贤令》、《谕普光寺僧众令》、《为文德圣皇后荐福令》等主要作品。

translation_en.user_profile: Li Zhi, also honored as Emperor Gaozong of Tang, was born on July 21, 628, in the Lizheng Hall of the East Palace at the Taiji Palace in Chang'an City. output.character_other_profile: She was born in Li Prefecture, Wenshui County, Bingzhou (modern-day Wenshui County, Shanxi Province) in 624 and died in the Shangyang Palace in Luoyang in 705. She reigned from 690 to 705, succeeding Emperor Ruizong of Tang and was succeeded by Emperor Zhongzong of Tang, Li Xian. Wu Zetian established the Zhou dynasty and instituted the imperial examination and military examinations, promoted agriculture and sericulture, and reformed the bureaucracy. Her major works include 'Compilation of Diligence in Administration,' 'Golden Wheel Compilation,' 'Ministerial Guidelines,' 'Lady of Fortune,' and 'Divine Palace Music.' She was a decisive and strong leader, ruthless yet open-minded, and liked listening to flattery. She worked with several ministers and officials, including Di Renjie, Su Weidao, Zhang Changzong, Zhang Yizhi, Xu Jingzhong, Prince Shu, Zhang Jianzhi, Li Yifu, Shangguan Yi, and Lai Junchen. Her adversaries included Empress Wang and rival consorts such as Consort Xiao and Consort Xiao Shu. Wu Zetian's children included Li Xian, Li Dan, and Princess Taiping, and her nephew was Wu Sansi. Regarding power, she believed women could rule like men and held that control in her own hands was most practical. Her lover was Li Zhi, and her former husband was Emperor Taizong of Tang.

user_profile: 台静农，本姓澹台，字伯简，原名传严，改名静农，笔名有青曲、孔嘉，是一位中国汉族的作家、文学评论家和书法家。他于1903年出生于安徽霍邱（今六安市叶集区）并在1990年去世。他曾在天津法政学院接受教育。在职业生涯中，他先后在辅仁大学、齐鲁大学、山东大学、厦门大学及四川江津女子师范学院任职，并最后在国立台湾大学担任教授。台静农的书法广泛涉及金文、刻石、碑版和各家墨迹，无论是篆、隶、草、行、楷等诸体皆精。除此之外，他还擅长篆刻和绘画。他的主要成就包括《地之子》、《建塔者》、《中国文学史》等代表作品，以及获得了国家文艺奖等荣誉。他的作品和艺术成就为世人所瞩目，有《台静农书艺集》及小说、散文等书出版。他的生活和事业，都在传播和提升中国文化的价值。

output.character_other_profile: 他是中国的知名近代作家，以其文体特征“鲁迅体”闻名，毕业于江南陆师学堂、东京弘文学院和日本仙台医学专门学校。他的代表作品包括《呐喊》、《彷徨》、《朝花夕拾》、《野草》、《华盖集》和《中国小说史略》等。鲁迅是中国现代文学的奠基人、中国翻译文学的开拓者、中国现代思想解放先驱和中国新兴版画运动的伟大导师，他在文学创作、文学批评、思想研究、文学史研究、翻译等多个领域具有重大贡献。他与台静农是好友，与戴季陶、郭沫若、梁启超和陈焕章是同僚，与刘半农是朋友。他曾翻译过《小约翰》，并以写作为特长。他的观点鲜明，例如他认为中国人的麻木不仁是刻在骨子里的，中国的革命需要拿起枪杆子，希望是不能抹杀的等。他的性格看得通透，被誉为先生、周老师、迅哥儿和老师，他的学生包括许广平。

translation_en.user_profile: Tai Jingnong, originally surnamed Tan Tai, courtesy name Bo Jian, originally named Chuan Yan, later renamed Jingnong, with pen names Qingqu and Kong Jia, was a Han Chinese writer, literary critic, and calligrapher. He was born in 1903 in Huoqiu, Anhui (now part of Yejie District, Lu'an), and passed away in 1990. He was educated at the Tianjin Legal and Political College. Throughout his career, he worked at Fu Jen Catholic University, Qilu University, Shandong University, Xiamen University, and Sichuan Jiangjin Women's Normal College, and eventually served as a professor at National Taiwan University. Tai Jingnong's calligraphy encompassed various scripts including seal, clerical, cursive, running, and regular styles, excelling in inscriptions and engravings. Besides, he was skilled in seal carving and painting. His major works include 'Children of the Earth,' 'The Tower Builder,' and 'History of Chinese Literature,' and he received the National Literary Award among other honors. His works and artistic achievements have been highly regarded, with publications including 'The Calligraphy of Tai Jingnong' and various novels and essays. His life and career were dedicated to promoting and enhancing the value of Chinese culture.

output.character_other_profile: He is a renowned modern Chinese writer, famous for his 'Lu Xun style' of writing. He graduated from Jiangnan Naval Academy, Tokyo Kobun College, and Sendai Medical College in Japan. His representative works include 'Call to Arms,' 'Wandering,' 'Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk,' 'Wild Grass,' 'The Grave,' and 'A Brief History of Chinese Fiction.' Lu Xun is a foundational figure in modern Chinese literature, a pioneer of Chinese translated literature, an avant-garde of modern Chinese thought liberation, and a great mentor of the emerging Chinese woodcut movement. He made significant contributions in literature creation, literary criticism, thought research, literary history research, translation, and more. He was friends with Tai Jingnong and colleagues with Dai Jitao, Guo Moruo, Liang Qichao, and Chen Huan Zhang, and had a friendship with Liu Bannong. He had translated 'Little John' and possessed a distinct writing ability. His views were clear, such as believing that Chinese apathy was ingrained, that revolution in China required armed struggle, and that hope could not be obliterated. He was perceptive and regarded as a teacher, known as Mr. Zhou, Teacher Zhou, Brother Xun, and a teacher of his students, including Xu Guangping.

translation_en.user_profile: Liu Bang, also known as Emperor Gaozu of Han, personal name Ji, posthumous title Emperor Gao, and temple name Taizu, was an outstanding politician and strategist in Chinese history and the founding emperor of the Han Dynasty. Born in 256 BC in Zhongyangli, Pei County, Jiangsu Province, he made significant contributions to the development of the Han people and the unification of China during the Warring States, Qin, and early Western Han periods. Liu Bang overthrew the Qin dynasty and defeated Chu, establishing the Han Dynasty and consolidating a unified empire. His notable works include 'The Song of the Great Wind' and 'The Song of the Swan.' He reigned from 202 BC until his death on June 1, 195 BC, and was buried in Changling. Historians have praised him through the ages, with Mao Zedong describing him as 'the most formidable among feudal emperors.'

Later, recommended by Xiao He to Liu Bang, Han Xin became a grand general. During the Chu-Han conflict, Han Xin showcased his exceptional military talents by conquering Wei, Dai, Zhao, Yan, and Qi. He completely annihilated Xiang Yu’s 200,000-strong Chu army at Weishui, forcing Xiang Yu to commit suicide. After the establishment of the Han dynasty, Han Xin was stripped of his military command, demoted to the King of Chu, later relegated to Marquis of Huaiyin, and was eventually executed in the Changle Palace. His life and deeds are recorded in the 'Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin.' He has been honored by later generations as the 'Immortal of War' and 'God of War,' and was praised by Liu Bang as 'invincible in battle, always victorious; I am not his equal.'

Lu Su held various official positions, including Grand Administrator of Hanchang and General of Hengjiang. His notable work is 'The Plan on the Couch.' In his life, Lu Su had a straightforward personality, was skilled in reading, riding, and shooting, and was known for his chivalry and generosity during times of chaos, often organizing local youths for military training. He pledged allegiance to Sun Quan in the second year of Jian'an and proposed strategic plans for him. During the Battle of Red Cliffs, he firmly supported the war effort alongside Zhou Yu, ultimately leading to a decisive defeat of Cao Cao's forces and establishing the tripartite division of the Three Kingdoms. After Zhou Yu's death, Sun Quan appointed Lu Su as Assistant Commander and successor to Zhou Yu, expanding the army to over ten thousand soldiers. Following the Battle of Red Cliffs, Lu Su was appointed Assistant Commander. However, negotiations with Guan Yu for the acquisition of Jingzhou were unsuccessful. He died in 217 at the age of 46, with Sun Quan personally presiding over his funeral, and Zhuge Liang also expressing condolences.

user_profile: 李治，别称小名雉奴，字号为善，是唐朝第三位皇帝，庙号为高宗，他在649年7月15日至683年12月27日在位。他出生于628年7月21日，于长安城太极宫的东宫之丽正殿，是唐太宗李世民第九子，其母为文德顺圣皇后长孙氏。他以晋王的身份起步，并在唐太宗的嫡长子太子李承乾与四子魏王李泰相继被废后，在643年被册立为皇太子。唐太宗去世后，李治即位为唐高宗，他在位期间，唐朝的版图扩大到了最大，从朝鲜半岛到咸海，从贝加尔湖到越南横山。他的主要成就包括开创了永徽之治，成功灭掉了高句丽和西突厥等国家。然而，由于健康问题，高宗在660年以后的政权逐渐由他转移到了武则天手中。他的主要作品有《监国求贤令》、《谕普光寺僧众令》、《为文德圣皇后荐福令》等。他于683年12月27日去世，享年五十五岁，葬于乾陵。他先后被谥号为天皇大帝、天皇大圣皇帝和天皇大圣大弘孝皇帝。

output.character_other_profile: He is a well-known modern Chinese writer, famous for his distinctive writing style known as 'Lu Xun style'. He graduated from Jiangnan Naval Academy, Tokyo Kobun Gakuin, and Sendai Medical College in Japan. His notable works include Call to Arms, Wandering, Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk, Wild Grass, Weeds, and A Brief History of Chinese Fiction. Lu Xun is a founding figure of Chinese modern literature, a pioneer of Chinese translated literature, a leading figure in the liberation of modern Chinese thought, and a great mentor of the modern Chinese woodcut movement. He made significant contributions in literature creation, literary criticism, ideological research, literary history research, and translation. He was friends with Tai Jingnong, and colleagues with Dai Jitao, Guo Moruo, Liang Qichao, and Chen Huan Zhang. He translated Little John and was known for his writing talent. His viewpoints were clear, such as his belief that apathy is ingrained in Chinese people, that China's revolution needs to take up arms, and that hope must not be extinguished, among others. He had a keen sense of insight, and was affectionately called Mr. Lu, Teacher Zhou, Brother Xun, and Teacher by his students, including Xu Guangping.

user_profile: 梅尧臣，字圣俞，也被人们尊称为宛陵先生，别名还包括梅直讲和梅都官。他出生于1002年5月31日，于宣州宣城，这是现在的安徽省宣城市宣州区。他是北宋时代的汉族官员以及现实主义诗人，是给事中梅询的从子。初任桐城主簿，后历任镇安军节度判官。在皇祐三年（1051年），他受到宋仁宗的召试，并赐予同进士出身，成为太常博士。他因受到欧阳修的推荐，成为国子监直讲，并累迁为尚书都官员外郎，因此他有时也被称为“梅直讲”和“梅都官”。1060年，梅尧臣去世，享年五十九岁。在诗歌创作方面，梅尧臣从少年时期就已展露才华，他与苏舜钦并齐，被时人并称为“苏梅”，与欧阳修齐名为“欧梅”。他主张诗歌写实，反对西昆体，他的诗歌力求平淡、含蓄，因此被誉为宋诗的“开山祖师”。他也曾参与编撰《新唐书》，并为《孙子兵法》作注。他的主要作品包括《宛陵集》以及《毛诗小传》等。此外，他也和'上竿鱼'的典故有关。

translation_en.character_profile: Ouyang Xiu, courtesy name Yongshu, also known by his alias Zuiweng and Ouyang Wenzhong, was a prominent politician and writer during the Northern Song Dynasty.
translation_en.user_profile: Mei Yaochen, courtesy name Shengyu, also respectfully called Mr. Wanling, had other aliases including Mei Zhijiang and Mei Duguan. He was born on May 31, 1002, in Xuanzhou, Xuancheng, which is now Xuanzhou District, Xuancheng, Anhui Province. He was a Han official and realist poet of the Northern Song era, and a descendant of Wei Zhong’s subordinate Mei Xun. He started his career as a registrar in Tongcheng, and later served as a military judge in the Zhenan Army. In the third year of Huangyou (1051), he was summoned by Emperor Renzong of Song for an imperial examination and was granted the degree of jinshi, becoming a Doctor of the Board of Rites. Thanks to Ouyang Xiu’s recommendation, he became a lecturer at the Directorate of Education and was eventually promoted to Secretary of the Ministry of Rites, thus also being referred to as ‘Mei Zhijiang’ and ‘Mei Duguan’. Mei Yaochen passed away in 1060 at the age of 59. In terms of poetry, Mei Yaochen exhibited his talent from a young age; he was paired with Su Shunqin as ‘Su Mei’ by contemporaries, and with Ouyang Xiu as ‘Ou Mei’. He advocated for realistic poetry and opposed the Xikun style. His poetry, striving for simplicity and implicitness, earned him fame as the founding figure of Song poetry. He also contributed to compiling the ‘New Tang Book’ and annotated ‘The Art of War’. His major works include ‘Collection from Wanling’ and ‘Little Commentary on Mao's Poetry’. Additionally, he is related to the idiom ‘Shanggan Fish’.
